note: Optional connectors a new OpenFlow install can set up. Generic on purpose: no private accounts, no credentials, no prices. Add an entry here and it shows up in the setup wizard and in Systems > Connections. Format and rules: platform/openflow-connectors.md.

connectors.name: Claude Code
connectors.summary: Anthropic's coding agent. Runs most of your team's agents.
connectors.headline: Run your agents on Claude
why: Most of the team's agents run on it, so this is the one to set up first
Signs in with your Claude account, so there is no key to copy
Agents can read, edit and test your code themselves
connectors.cost: Included with a Claude subscription plan. Without a plan you pay Anthropic per use through an API key.

steps: Install it (press Run it for me, or copy the command).
Open a terminal and run: claude
Choose your Claude account when it asks you to sign in, then finish in the browser.

connectors.name: Codex
connectors.summary: OpenAI's coding agent. Lets you run GPT-based agents next to the Claude ones.
connectors.headline: Add GPT-based agents to the team
why: A second opinion from a different family of models
Signs in with your ChatGPT account
Mix it with Claude agents in the same channel
connectors.cost: Included with a ChatGPT plan that offers Codex. Otherwise pay OpenAI per use through an API key.

steps: Install it (press Run it for me, or copy the command).
Run: codex login
Finish the sign-in in the browser window it opens.

connectors.name: Antigravity (Gemini)
connectors.summary: Google's agent CLI. Runs Gemini-based agents.
connectors.headline: Add Gemini-based agents
why: Brings Google's models to your team
Signs in with your Google account
Handy for big files and long documents
connectors.cost: Uses your Google account. Limits depend on the plan you hold with Google.

steps: Install it (command below; it comes from Google).
Run: agy
Sign in with your Google account when the browser opens. On a server it prints a link to open on your own computer.

connectors.name: OpenRouter
connectors.summary: One key for hundreds of models from many companies.
connectors.headline: One key for hundreds of models
why: Try many models without opening an account with each company
One bill instead of many
Switch an agent's model without new setup
connectors.cost: Pay per use, at each model's own rate. You top up a balance first.

steps: Press Get an OpenRouter key. Sign in or create an account; it brings you straight to Keys.
Add a little credit if it asks, create a key and copy it.
Come back here and press Paste and save.

connectors.name: xAI (Grok)
connectors.summary: Grok models from xAI.
connectors.headline: Grok models for your agents
why: Adds Grok as another model choice
Pay only for what agents use
Keep it as a backup when another provider is down
connectors.cost: Pay per use through your xAI account.

steps: Press Get an xAI key. Sign in or create an account, and add credit.
Open API Keys, create a key and copy it.
Come back here and press Paste and save.

connectors.name: DeepSeek
connectors.summary: DeepSeek models, usually the cheapest way to run a busy agent.
connectors.headline: Low-cost models for busy agents
why: Often the cheapest way to keep an agent running all day
Good for routine work that doesn't need a top model
Pay only for what is used
connectors.cost: Pay per use through your DeepSeek account.

steps: Press Get a DeepSeek key. Sign in or create an account, and add credit.
Create a key and copy it.
Come back here and press Paste and save.

connectors.name: OpenAI API
connectors.summary: For tools that call OpenAI directly, such as image generation.
connectors.headline: Let your tools call OpenAI directly
why: Needed for image generation and other tools that use the OpenAI API
Separate from a ChatGPT subscription
Pay only for what is used
connectors.cost: Pay per use through your OpenAI API account. This is separate from a ChatGPT plan.

steps: Press Get an OpenAI key. Sign in; billing must be set up.
Create a key and copy it.
Come back here and press Paste and save.

connectors.name: Ollama (models on your own computer)
connectors.summary: Runs open models on your own machine. Nothing leaves your computer.
connectors.headline: Run AI models on your own computer
why: Nothing leaves your machine, so it is private
No per-use cost once a model is downloaded
Works offline
connectors.cost: Free. It uses your own hardware, so a graphics card helps.

steps: Install Ollama (command below, or the installer from ollama.com).
Download a model, for example: ollama pull llama3.2
It listens on port 11434. This page shows Running when it is up.

connectors.name: Filesystem tools
connectors.summary: Lets agents read and write inside one folder you choose.
connectors.headline: Give agents a folder to work in
why: Agents can read and write files in just the folder you pick
Nothing outside that folder is touched
Quick to add, quick to remove
connectors.cost: Free.

steps: Choose the folder agents may use.
Press Add. It is added to your MCP list; agents pick it up the next time they start.

connectors.name: Browser control (Playwright)
connectors.summary: Lets agents open pages, click, fill forms and take screenshots in a real browser.
connectors.headline: Let agents use a real browser
why: Agents can open pages, click, fill in forms and screenshot the result
Lets them test the websites they build
Free, and it downloads its own browser
connectors.cost: Free.

steps: Press Add. It is added to your MCP list; agents pick it up the next time they start.
The first use downloads a browser, which takes a minute.

connectors.name: Library docs (Context7)
connectors.summary: Gives agents current documentation for code libraries instead of what they remember.
connectors.headline: Current docs for any code library
why: Stops agents guessing from out-of-date memory
Fewer broken examples and wrong function names
Free to use
connectors.cost: Free tier. Heavy use needs an account with Upstash.

steps: Press Add. It is added to your MCP list; agents pick it up the next time they start.

connectors.name: Simple memory
connectors.summary: A small notebook agents can write facts into and look things up from. No database needed.
connectors.headline: A simple notebook for agents
why: Agents write facts down and look them up later
No database to install
A good first step before shared memory search
connectors.cost: Free.

steps: Press Add. It is added to your MCP list; agents pick it up the next time they start.

connectors.name: Step-by-step thinking
connectors.summary: Helps an agent break a hard problem into steps and revise them.
connectors.headline: Help agents think a problem through
why: Breaks a hard problem into steps an agent can revise
Cuts down on rushed, half-finished answers
Free to use
connectors.cost: Free.

steps: Press Add. It is added to your MCP list; agents pick it up the next time they start.

connectors.name: Supabase (database tools)
connectors.summary: Lets agents read and change a Supabase project's tables and settings.
connectors.headline: Let agents work with your database
why: Agents can read and change tables and settings in a Supabase project
Saves you copying SQL back and forth
You choose which project it can see
connectors.cost: The tool is free. Supabase itself has a free tier and paid plans.

steps: Press Get a Supabase access token. Sign in, generate a token and copy it.
Come back here, press Paste and save, then press Add. Use a development project, not live data.

connectors.name: Shared memory search (Qdrant)
connectors.summary: Searchable team memory: agents store what they learn and find it again later. Needs a Qdrant database running.
connectors.headline: Team memory that agents can search
why: Agents store what they learn and find it again later
Your team stops solving the same problem twice
Runs on your own computer
connectors.cost: Free. Qdrant runs on your own machine in Docker.

steps: Start Qdrant (press Run it for me, or copy the command). It needs Docker.
Press Add. The tool needs Python's uv installed (astral.sh/uv).
Agents pick it up the next time they start.

connectors.name: Higgsfield
connectors.summary: Image and video generation from your agents.
connectors.headline: Make images and video from your agents
why: Agents can generate pictures and clips for you
Handy for mock-ups, social posts and demos
Signs in with your Higgsfield account
connectors.cost: Needs a paid Higgsfield plan. Every job uses credits, and the free plan has none.

steps: Press Add to put the Higgsfield tool in your MCP list.
The first time an agent uses it, it gives a link. Open it and sign in to your Higgsfield account.
Optional command line: npm install -g @higgsfield/cli, then higgsfield auth login.

connectors.name: fal.ai
connectors.summary: Fast image, video and audio models behind one key.
connectors.headline: Fast image, video and audio models
why: Many models behind a single key
Quick results, so agents aren't left waiting
Pay only for what is used
connectors.cost: Pay per use. You buy credit first.

steps: Press Get a fal key. Sign in or create an account, and add credit.
Create a key and copy it.
Come back here and press Paste and save.

connectors.name: Replicate
connectors.summary: Thousands of community image, video and audio models.
connectors.headline: Thousands of community AI models
why: Pick from a huge library of image, video and audio models
Try a model before you commit to it
Pay only for what is used
connectors.cost: Pay per use, billed by the second the model runs.

steps: Press Get a Replicate token. Sign in or create an account, and add a payment method.
Create a token and copy it.
Come back here and press Paste and save.

connectors.name: Pexels (stock photos and video)
connectors.summary: Free stock photos and clips agents can search and download.
connectors.headline: Free stock photos and video
why: Agents can find and download pictures and clips for a project
Free to use under Pexels' licence
No cost for the key
connectors.cost: Free. Rate limits apply.

steps: Press Get a Pexels key. Sign in or create a free account and fill in the short form; the key is instant.
Copy the key.
Come back here and press Paste and save.

connectors.name: GitHub
connectors.summary: Lets agents clone, branch, push and open pull requests.
connectors.headline: Let agents work with your code on GitHub
why: Agents can clone, branch, push and open pull requests
Your code stays backed up and shareable
You stay in charge: review before anything is merged
connectors.cost: Free for personal and small-team use.

steps: Install the GitHub command line tool, gh (cli.github.com).
Run: gh auth login
Choose GitHub.com, then your browser, and finish there.

connectors.name: Cloudflare (Wrangler)
connectors.summary: Publish sites and small back ends to Cloudflare.
connectors.headline: Publish sites with Cloudflare
why: Put a website or small back end online from the terminal
Fast worldwide, with a free starting tier
Agents can deploy for you
connectors.cost: Free tier. Paid plans for heavy use.

steps: Install it (press Run it for me, or copy the command).
Run: wrangler login
Approve access in the browser.

connectors.name: Netlify
connectors.summary: Publish websites to Netlify.
connectors.headline: Publish websites with Netlify
why: Put a site online with one command
Preview links for every change
Agents can deploy for you
connectors.cost: Free tier. Paid plans for heavy use.

steps: Install it (press Run it for me, or copy the command).
Run: netlify login
Approve access in the browser.

connectors.name: Vercel
connectors.summary: Publish websites and Next.js apps to Vercel.
connectors.headline: Publish Next.js apps with Vercel
why: Built for Next.js, and fine for any web app
Preview links for every change
Agents can deploy for you
connectors.cost: Free tier for personal projects. Paid plans for teams and heavy use.

steps: Install it (press Run it for me, or copy the command).
Run: vercel login
Approve access in the browser.

connectors.name: Supabase command line
connectors.summary: Run a Supabase database on your own machine and manage projects from the terminal.
connectors.headline: Run a database on your own computer
why: Full Supabase stack for building and testing, with nothing online
Manage projects from the terminal
Agents can set up and migrate for you
connectors.cost: Free. Hosted Supabase projects have their own plans.

steps: Install it by the method for your system (link below). It also needs Docker for a local database.
To use a hosted project, run: supabase login

connectors.name: Resend (send email)
connectors.summary: Lets your apps and agents send email from your own domain.
connectors.headline: Send email from your own domain
why: Your apps and agents can send real email
Replies and receipts come from your address
A free tier is enough to start
connectors.cost: Free tier with a monthly sending limit. Paid plans above it.

steps: Press Get a Resend key. Sign in or create an account (verify your sending domain if you will send from it).
Create a key with sending access and copy it.
Come back here and press Paste and save.

connectors.name: n8n (workflow automation)
connectors.summary: Draw workflows that connect your apps, then let agents trigger them.
connectors.headline: Draw workflows that connect your apps
why: Join apps together without writing code
Agents can trigger a workflow when something happens
Runs on your own computer
connectors.cost: Free to run yourself. n8n also sells a hosted version.

steps: Start n8n (press Run it for me, or copy the command). It needs Docker.
Open http://localhost:5678 and create your owner account. This page shows Running when it is up.

connectors.name: TypeSafe Jev
connectors.headline: Smart skill hints for your agents
connectors.summary: A very fast, cheap checker that tells an agent which skill its task probably needs. This connection also unlocks the skill hints option.
why: Agents are nudged to the right skill instead of having to know every skill
Checks a message in about a fifth of a second
Off until you switch it on; it only adds one line to a message, which the agent can ignore
connectors.cost: Pay per use, a tiny fraction of a cent for each message checked. You top up a balance first.

steps: Press Get a TypeSafe key. Sign in or create an account and open the API keys page.
Add a little credit if it asks, create a key and copy it.
Come back here and press Paste and save. Then switch on skill hints.

connectors.name: WhatsApp Switchboard
connectors.headline: One WhatsApp link for all your services
connectors.summary: A local service that links to your WhatsApp as a linked device, so your assistants can use it with their own keys and limits. Off until you switch it on.
why: One connection, with a separate key and set of limits for every service that uses it
A kill switch, an audit log with no message text, and held deletes you can cancel
Contacts are sorted by type, so each service only sees the people it should
connectors.cost: Free. It is an unofficial linked-device connection, so WhatsApp may limit or ban an account that sends a lot. For business messaging, the official WhatsApp Business API is the safer choice.

steps: Read the warning first: this is an unofficial connection, so keep it to light, personal use.
Start the service. It is off by default. This page shows Running when it is up.
Open the WhatsApp page in DevFlow, then scan the QR code from Linked devices on your phone.
